title: Fastpath NetProof: Operator Handbook (PRD sketch)
content:
Goal: provide a concise operator-facing PRD sketch for a low-friction, cryptographically-sound evidence path used during customer-managed VPC handoffs and minor network changes. Focus: reduce human friction for onboarding while preserving a minimal audit trace that satisfies compliance reviewers and expedited troubleshooting.

Context / why this exists:
- Customers repeatedly ask for a way to onboard small network changes without full attestation pipelines and without shipping large audit blobs.
- Ops teams need a standard that: (1) is easy to produce client-side, (2) is verifiable by Redwood control-plane, and (3) is small enough to store for short-term retention tiers.
- This doc sits between: self-hosted full attestation (heavy, slow) and no-proof fast onramp (risky).

Non-goals:
- Replace full forensic evidence sets for major infra changes.
- Provide legally-binding long-term evidence for enterprise eDiscovery.

Audience:
- Redwood operator oncall / onboarding engineer
- Solutions engineer guiding customer PoC
- Product PM owning Private deployment UX

Design principles (ops-centric):
1) Minimal: evidence must be small (<= 10KB typical) and serializable as JSON or compact binary.
2) Verifiable: include signer identity (customer or operator), monotonic change id, and a deterministic hash over key artifacts.
3) Fast: generation takes <5s on customer side; upload + verification <15s.
4) Graceful rollback: if verification fails, system offers clear fallback (retry, snapshot, full attestation).

Core artifact: CompactChangeRecord (CCR)
- Fields (flattened, human-mappable):
  - change_id: short human + hex (e.g. "cust-20240912-7f4a")
  - parent_snapshot_hash: hex OR null for initial onboarding
  - summary: 1-line natural language summary (free text)
  - affected_paths: list of strings (e.g., CIDR, route-table id, firewall rule id) [limit 10 entries]
  - timestamp_utc: ISO8601
  - signer: {type, id} -> flattened as signer_type and signer_id strings (see note)
  - signature_scheme: string (e.g., ed25519-v1)
  - signature: base64
  - evidence_digest: hex (sha256 of any attached payloads)
  - retention_class: one of [fastpath-7d, standard-90d, archival-365d]
  - human_notes: short text (optional, max 500 chars)

Operator UX sketch (runbook):
1) Customer triggers a small change via UI or agent. Change is validated locally against onboard policy template.
2) Agent builds CCR, signs with either customer operator key or a delegated short-lived operator token (delegated signing is optional).
3) CCR uploaded to control-plane endpoint /v1/private/ccr (multipart upload allowed for small attachments).
4) Control plane runs lightweight verification: schema, signature check, retention-class quota check, policy heuristics.
5) If OK, control-plane returns decision = {accepted, sampling_bucket}.
6) Operator console shows green + link to snapshot + short digest view.
7) In failure modes, control-plane returns human-readable error and recommended remediation: (a) re-run signing, (b) escalate to full attestation, (c) opens support ticket template.

Sample CCR (compact JSON, truncated):
{
  "change_id": "cust-20240912-7f4a",
  "parent_snapshot_hash": "f3a1...",
  "summary": "Add egress route for analytics collectors",
  "affected_paths": ["vpc-rtb-003:route-analytics"],
  "timestamp_utc": "2024-09-12T18:03:12Z",
  "signer_type": "customer-kms",
  "signer_id": "projects/acme/keys/edge-op",
  "signature_scheme": "ed25519-v1",
  "signature": "BASE64SIG...",
  "evidence_digest": "c5b2...",
  "retention_class": "fastpath-7d",
  "human_notes": "temporary open for analytics pump, will tighten 9/14"
}

Retention / storage model (ops notes):
- fastpath-7d: raw CCR preserved + tiny metadata index. Stored for 7 days. Default for minor changes. Low-cost compressed storage. No attachments unless operator opts in.
- standard-90d: CCR + optional attachments (up to 1MB). Stored 90 days. Good for medium risk changes.
- archival-365d: full evidence bundle (attachments allowed up to 50MB), sig metadata and escrow token. For compliance-heavy customers (paid).

Approval gate matrix (simplified):
- low-risk: fastpath-7d automatic accept if agent signed and heuristics pass. No human approval.
- medium-risk: standard-90d, require secondary signer (operator or delegated reviewer) OR a canary window (10m).
- high-risk: archival-365d, block unless explicit SRE/prod approval ticket exists.

Sampling & observability:
- Keep 5% of fastpath-7d into long-term sampling bucket (standard-90d) for regression detection. Sampling deterministic by change_id hash.
- Metrics to surface: CCR acceptance rate, signature failures, retention_class per-customer, median verification latency, number of escalations.
- Quick dashboard: /console/private/onramp/fastpath-metrics

Audit log schema (for operator debugging):
- event_time, change_id, customer_id, decision, verifier_version, signature_valid (true/false), retention_class, verdict_reason, control_plane_tx_id
- Example line (CSV): 2024-09-12T18:03:13Z,cust-7f4a,acme,accepted,v1.2,true,fastpath-7d,heuristics-passed,tx-0001

Operator playbook (step-by-step):
- Pre-onboarding: check customer has an up-to-date short-term signing key and that agent policy template exists. If missing, run onboarding wizard. (Ticket template: JIRA-PD-981)
- During onramp: monitor verification latency, if >2s for 3 consecutive CCRs escalate to infra team (label: netproof-latency).
- Post-change: confirm sampled CCRs are archived to standard-90d, notify CS for any customer queries.

Failure modes and remediation notes (short):
- signature_mismatch: ask customer to rotate key and re-sign; provide debug script.
- schema_error: return exact field error and link to CCR schema doc.
- quota_exceeded: promote retention_class to a paid tier or require purge.
- attack suspicion (replay/duplicate change_id): escalate to SRE + forensics runbook.

Open questions / TODOs:
- signing: customer KMS vs ephemeral operator token — decide default for self-serve flows. (PM decision needed)
- sampling rate: should we make it configurable per-customer? default 5% OK but ops needs quick override.
- legal: are fastpath-7d traces usable in SOC2 request? Seems unlikely; lawyer confirm. (Legal: contact Nora Patel)
- storage cost model: build estimator into console onboarding with real price delta.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Alpha (internal): enable for Redwood-managed test accounts only. Run with ops oncall; collect metrics.
2) Beta (select customers): onboard 3 customers via solutions eng. Measure success criteria: mean verification latency <500ms, <1% escalations.
3) GA: open to self-serve with default retention choices visible in console and billing controls.

Testing checklist for SRE (preprod):
- fuzz CCRs and ensure deterministic verifier rejects malformed but accepts valid.
- simulate replay attack (same change_id twice) -> verifier should reject second unless parent_snapshot changed.
- load test: 10k CCRs/min with 50% attachments -> measure p99 latency and storage ingestion pipeline.

References and links:
- CCR schema (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/netproof-protos/blob/main/ccr.proto
- Onboarding wizard (design mock): https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=fastpath-mock
- Support ticket template: JIRA-PD-981

Notes to self (choppy):
- prefer ed25519 for simplicity and client libs.
- short retention helps sales close low-risk customers quickly.
- keep manual approval path obvious in console (big red button = escalate to full attestation).

Action items:
- [Evelyn] finalize schema + minimal sample CCRs (due 2024-10-01)
- [Diego] prototype verifier service + benchmark (due 2024-11-01)
- [Aisha] draft customer-facing FAQ and onboarding copy (due 2024-10-15)
- [Marta] coordinate legal on SOC2 usability question (due 2024-10-10)

End of sketch.
